status_definitions.compiled_exact: The source claim is represented by a compiled source-facing theorem with the same mathematical content.
status_definitions.compiled_equivalent: The source claim is compiled under a semantically equivalent encoding; representation changes are documented.
status_definitions.compiled_by_composition: All essential clauses are compiled, but the source result is assembled from multiple declarations rather than one literal wrapper.
status_definitions.compiled_generalized: A compiled theorem is strictly more general or gives a stronger conclusion than the printed source claim.
status_definitions.compiled_specialization: A useful compiled specialization exists, but it does not cover the full printed source scope.
status_definitions.compiled_stronger_hypotheses: The source conclusion is compiled, but the current theorem uses additional or stronger hypotheses.
status_definitions.compiled_source_repair: The source is internally inconsistent or contains a false/overbroad clause; the formalization records the mathematically usable repaired statement.
status_definitions.compiled_role_replaced: The exact source proof lemma is not exposed as a theorem; its role in the main proof is discharged by a different compiled argument. This is not exact source-item coverage.
status_definitions.not_represented: No matching formal theorem or construction was found.
status_definitions.not_proof_debt: The item is exposition, empirical methodology, or an extension beyond the paper theorem surface; it is documented but not counted as missing source theorem coverage.

verification_definitions.proved_in_build: Every cited Lean declaration exists in the repository and is part of the package tree that the user has reported building successfully.
verification_definitions.absent: No matching Lean declaration is cited because the source claim is not represented.
verification_definitions.not_applicable: No proof is required for this row.

semantic_alignment_definitions.exact: Source and Lean claim have the same mathematical hypotheses and conclusion, modulo notation.
semantic_alignment_definitions.equivalent_encoding: The mathematical claim is equivalent; Lean changes representation or packages assumptions differently.
semantic_alignment_definitions.by_composition: The source claim is recovered from a chain of compiled declarations rather than one wrapper.
semantic_alignment_definitions.generalized: Lean proves a stronger or more general result.
semantic_alignment_definitions.specialized: Lean proves only a restricted source case.
semantic_alignment_definitions.stronger_hypotheses: Lean proves the source conclusion but assumes more.
semantic_alignment_definitions.source_repair: Lean intentionally formalizes a repaired reading of inconsistent/false source prose.

semantic_alignment_definitions.missing: No corresponding Lean result was found.
semantic_alignment_definitions.out_of_scope: The row is tracked for context but is not a source theorem obligation.

paper.citation: Aranyak Acharyya, Michael W. Trosset, Carey E. Priebe, Hayden Helm, Consistent estimation of generative model representations in the Data Kernel Perspective Space, arXiv:2409.17308.
paper.source_version: Retained arXiv transcription in Acharyya2024/prose; audit is keyed to the theorem/assumption numbering in that source.

scope: Finite raw-stress/MDS setup and the numbered consistency surface used downstream: Remark 1--3 where they carry mathematical content, Theorems 1--5, Assumptions 1--2, Lemmas 1--2, and Corollary 1. Empirical sections are excluded.
audit_revision: 2026-08-28; A24-T2 and A24-T4 reclassified exact and A24-T5 assembled over the population law. Appendix A.2 is discharged through the response matrix, row by row over the queries, so no concentration theorem takes a second-moment bound as an input any more. The growing-model theorems no longer carry a rate shared by the whole model collection; each model has its own. The passage from a drawn-model population to the joint law is by domination, not by uniformity.
notes:
Source coverage is complete for the numbered surface in scope, and the remaining distance is recorded per row rather than in the aggregate. Four printed claims are refuted with compiled counterexamples: Corollary 1's alignment quantifier, Theorem 1's fixed limiting profile without a uniqueness premise, Remark 1's description of the invariance as affine, and, for the one-point stress, the necessity of an identifiability premise. Each refutation is accompanied by the repaired statement. The UniquePairProfile premise is therefore a source repair, not a hypothesis added to the paper: its necessity is machine-checked.

The continuum model-distribution layer is formalized -- continuous raw stress, the minimizer set, the out-of-sample map in a common frame, and the continuous-MDS identification the source attributes to its reference [23]. Lemma 2 is proved for the empirical model distribution and over the population law, with the estimate fitted to the sample dissimilarities as printed, with the subsequence produced rather than assumed and independent of the tolerance, and with the identically-distributed hypothesis derived from the source's own definition of D rather than assumed. Theorem 5 composes it with Theorem 4 over the population law.

Theorems 2 and 4 are exact: the passage from the paper's definition of gamma to the sample-mean second-moment bound -- its Appendix A.2 -- is discharged rather than assumed, row by row over the queries, needing replicate independence for each fixed query and nothing across queries.

ONE REPAIR REMAINS, and it is in the sampling model rather than in any theorem: the source declares the latent vectors phi_i iid while the estimate depends on model-specific response laws and on sampled responses, so the printed integral does not denote anything under a measure on the latent space alone. The formalization augments the inner population measure by the response outcome. That is a choice among possible repairs, not the unique minimal one; A24-T5 records what was chosen and what was not.

fixed-profile-uniqueness.title: The paper fixes one limiting MDS profile without a uniqueness premise -- REFUTED
fixed-profile-uniqueness.detail:
Theorem 1, Lemma 1, and Theorem 3 name a fixed limiting minimizer/profile. Lean proves unconditional convergence to the minimizer set, and recovers a fixed profile only under RawStress.UniquePairProfile. Under that premise Lean gets full-sequence convergence, stronger than the source subsequence conclusion.

REFUTED, with a machine-checked counterexample. Acharyya2024.ProfileNonuniqueness.no_fixed_limiting_profile exhibits a sequence of dissimilarity matrices converging in probability to the equilateral matrix on three objects -- constantly equal to it -- and a selection of raw-stress minimizers for which no subsequence and no minimizer of the limit make the pairwise distances converge in probability. Every hypothesis of the printed theorem holds in its strongest form.

The obstruction is structural, not exotic. Raw stress sees the dissimilarity matrix only through its entries, so a matrix invariant under relabeling the models has a minimizer set closed under relabeling. Three points on a line cannot be mutually equidistant unless they coincide, and coinciding is not optimal against the equilateral matrix, so relabeling yields a genuinely different pairwise-distance profile. A selection returning one labeling on half the sample points and the other on the rest defeats every fixed profile.

RawStress.UniquePairProfile is exactly what rules this out. The package's extra hypothesis is therefore a repair of the source, not an assumption added to it, and the rows carrying it are dispositioned accordingly.

growing-query-rate-wiring.title: RESOLVED -- the growing-query gamma/r condition is wired end to end
growing-query-rate-wiring.detail:
ORIGINAL FINDING. The second-moment and probability modules proved the finite-dimensional concentration mechanism and the gamma/r sample-mean estimate, but Lean fed the growing-query consistency theorem an abstract sampling-convergence hypothesis rather than constructing the varying-m response matrices and discharging the source rate condition in one theorem.

STATUS: closed. dissimilarity_convergesInProbability_of_replicates constructs nothing abstract: it takes the replicates, their means and their trace-covariances, and the source's ((1/m) sum_i sum_j gamma_ij)/r -> 0, and concludes Frobenius convergence in probability. pointwise_dissimilarity_convergesInProbability_of_replicates is the growing-model counterpart and lp_consistency_of_replicates_population carries it through to the Theorem 5 endpoint. See growing-n-concentration for how Appendix A.2 is discharged.

rigid-alignment-corollary.title: RESOLVED -- Corollary 1's coordinate alignment is represented in both modes
rigid-alignment-corollary.detail:
The source upgrades pairwise-distance convergence to existence of orthogonal W^(u) and translations a^(u) with point-coordinate convergence. Acharyya2024 proves translation invariance and pairwise-distance convergence but has no theorem constructing the source Corollary 1 alignment.

Done. Both modes are now proved: almost surely via ae_eventually_exists_rigidMotion_of_ae_pairDist_tendsto, and in probability via tendsto_measure_alignmentError_of_pairDist_convergesInProbability and tendsto_measure_alignedConfig_dist_gt. The in-probability mode needed a modulus uniform over configurations, since the sample point is not fixed when the tolerance is chosen; that is TauCeti.exists_delta_forall_exists_rigidMotion.

continuous-mds-lp.title: RESOLVED -- the continuum layer, including the sample-dissimilarity perturbation the printed lemma states
continuous-mds-lp.detail:
ORIGINAL FINDING. The source introduces a compact model space, a model distribution P, continuous raw stress as an integral functional, and an mds map, then states Lemma 2 and Theorem 5 as L^p(P x P) convergence. None of that existed in the package: there was no model distribution, no continuous raw stress and no mds map, so the printed conclusions could not be written down at all.

STATUS: the chain is complete, end to end, including the sample-dissimilarity perturbation. What follows is the current state, not a history.

  Definitions. continuousRawStress is the source's double integral and ContinuousMDS its minimizer set over Borel-measurable embeddings -- a set rather than a chosen map, since MDS determines an embedding only up to a rigid motion. continuousRawStress_empiricalPopulation ties it to the package's finite rawStress through TauCeti's empirical measure, so it extends the finite notion rather than competing with it. lpPairDistErr is the L^p(P x P) discrepancy the conclusions are about, and lpPairDistErr_rigidMotion_left/_right record why it, and not a coordinatewise error, is the well-posed quantity.

  The estimated embedding as a map on the model space. Lemma 2 integrates over P x P, so the estimate must be defined at arbitrary models. frameEmbedding places every model against one fixed reference configuration by minimizing pointStress, the one-point raw stress. exists_min_pointStress proves the minimum is attained (continuous plus coercive), norm_min_pointStress_le_of_bounded bounds minimizers by 4K independently of sample size, and pointStress_rigidMotion shows the pairwise distances do not depend on the frame chosen.

  The population counterpart. continuousPointStress is the population one-point stress and exists_min_continuousPointStress proves its minimum attained, by a dominated-convergence continuity argument and coercivity.

  The limit theorems. ae_tendsto_averaged_pointStress is the strong law for the averaged one-point stress; the null set it produces depends on the position, and tendsto_of_dense_of_equiLipschitz spreads convergence from a countable dense set to the whole space off a SINGLE null set, using abs_sub_pointStress_le, whose Lipschitz constant does not grow with the sample. eventually_forall_isMinOn_dist_lt then moves the minimizer SET -- for every tolerance, eventually EVERY minimizer of the stage objective lies within it of the limit. Because it names no particular minimizer, no measurable selection is needed anywhere: TauCeti.measurableSet_exists_isMinOn_le makes the one-stage minimizer event measurable, since being a minimizer is a sublevel condition on a measurable infimum, and TauCeti.measurableSet_tendsto_isMinOn assembles the convergence event from countably many of those.

  The moving target. ae_eventually_forall_isMinOn_of_iid minimizes against the population dissimilarities. The printed estimate minimizes against the SAMPLE dissimilarities, which are only assumed to approach them, so ae_eventually_forall_isMinOn_of_iid_target lets the target be an arbitrary array that changes with the stage. Its proof is the same one: abs_sub_pointStress_target bounds the change in the one-point stress by the average target error times a bound depending only on the position, so pointwise convergence survives, while the equi-Lipschitz estimate and the 4K minimizer bound only ever used the uniform bound on the target, which the moving target still satisfies. The theorem runs along a subsequence, which is where the printed lemma's own subsequence goes.

  The conclusions. tendsto_measure_lpPairDistErr_population reaches the printed convergence-in-probability mode by the expectation route, exchanging no quantifiers: the expectation of the L^p discrepancy over the sample is, by Tonelli, the double integral of the per-pair expectations; each vanishes by dominated convergence against the uniform bound; and Markov converts the vanishing expectation into convergence in probability. It needs only joint measurability of the integrand -- the condition the printed statement needs for its own integral to denote anything. tendsto_measure_lpPairDistErr_sampleTarget is the printed Lemma 2 with the estimate fitted to the sample dissimilarities, and exists_subseq_tendsto_measure_lpPairDistErr_of_identical states it under a hypothesis on the dissimilarities alone, producing the subsequence itself.

  Why the printed hypothesis needed repairing, with a witness. Read literally, "for all pairs (i, i') in N x N, D_ii' ->P Delta(phi_i, phi_i')" does not control a GROWING collection: TauCeti.exists_triangular_array_tendsto_pointwise_average_eq_half exhibits a bounded array whose entries are eventually zero at every fixed index while the average is exactly one half at every stage. What repairs it is already implicit in the sampling model -- at each stage the errors are the same statistic applied to interchangeable models, hence identically distributed. TauCeti.exists_subseq_ae_tendsto_average_of_tendsto_measure_ge is that argument: identical distribution makes the mean of the average equal the mean of a single error, TauCeti.tendsto_integral_of_tendsto_measure_ge_of_bounded turns bounded convergence in probability into L^1 convergence, and TauCeti.exists_subseq_ae_tendsto_zero_of_tendsto_integral passes to a subsequence. The subsequence is not a weakness of the argument and not an artifact of this formalization; L^1 convergence does not give almost-everywhere convergence, which is precisely why the printed lemma has one too.

  The identifiability premise. The argmin steps assume the limiting one-point stress has a unique minimizer. Consistency.not_unique_min_continuousPointStress shows that cannot be dropped: two reference points at distance two with target dissimilarity two from each give a stress minimized at three separate places, and constant sequences at two of them converge to different limits. The premise is therefore a repair of the source, on the same footing as RawStress.UniquePairProfile.

  Generality of the encoding. The dissimilarities are a function of the drawn model sequence rather than of separate data. That costs nothing: a model that carries its own replicate data is a point of a larger model space, and every hypothesis is stated for an arbitrary measurable space.

TWO CLAUSES COME OUT STRONGER THAN PRINTED: one statement in p rather than one per p, and, for the population-target form tendsto_measure_lpPairDistErr_outOfSample, the full sequence rather than a subsequence.

CORRECTIONS MADE WHILE WORKING, recorded so the reasoning can be checked rather than trusted. An earlier version of this entry named a law of large numbers for V-statistics as the missing foundation; that was wrong, because the population form integrates against P x P, so Fubini removes the double average entirely. The V-statistic results built then (TauCeti.map_evalPair_pi, TauCeti.integral_doubleSum_pi) are correct and reusable but are not on this critical path. The out-of-sample map was first defined by augmenting one model at a time, which gives each model its own frame and cannot serve an integral comparing two models; frameEmbedding replaced it. A composition attempt did not compile because the integrand was a let-bound local abbreviation and the unifier looped; lifting it to the top-level pairDiscrepancy fixed that. And this row was once recorded as closed while the estimate was still fitted to the population dissimilarities rather than the sample ones -- that claim was withdrawn, and closing it properly is what the moving-target theorem above does.

UPDATE (2026-08-28). Two things in the paragraphs above are now weaker than what is proved, and one sentence in them was wrong. The identically-distributed hypothesis is no longer assumed: integral_absPairErr_eq_of_dissimilarityFactors derives it from the source's own definition of D as a statistic of the two models involved, and exists_subseq_tendsto_measure_lpPairDistErr_of_pairwise is the lemma with that factorization in place of the assumption. The subsequence is produced before the tolerance is chosen, so one subsequence serves every tolerance, as printed; the earlier statement quantified the tolerance first, which was weaker than the construction. And the sentence claiming that a model carrying its own replicate data 'costs nothing' understated the matter: it is precisely the repair, since the source declares only the latent vectors iid. The printed conclusion does not denote anything otherwise, so some repair is forced, but augmenting the inner population measure by the response outcome is a choice among repairs. A24-T5 records the choice and the alternative.

affine-invariance-partial.title: Remark 1's invariance is rigid, not affine -- now proved and the wording corrected
affine-invariance-partial.detail:
rawStress_translate proves the translation component. No Acharyya2024 theorem explicitly packages the orthogonal part of the rigid transformation or the full source wording. The paper calls this affine, while its later Corollary 1 uses orthogonal W plus translation.

Done, with a correction. RawStress.rawStress_rigidMotion and RawStress.mds_rigidMotion package the full orthogonal-plus-translation statement: raw stress is unchanged by a rigid motion and the minimizer set is closed under them. The source's word 'affine' is too wide, and rawStress_not_affine_invariant shows it: a dilation changes every distance and therefore the stress. The paper's own Corollary 1 uses an orthogonal map plus a translation, which is the correct class, so this is a wording slip rather than a mathematical error.

growing-n-concentration.title: RESOLVED -- growing-query and growing-model concentration, from the source's gamma
growing-n-concentration.detail:
ORIGINAL FINDING. The finite second-moment concentration theorem handled any fixed finite model set, and the triangular-array consistency theorem assumed per-stage dissimilarity convergence outright, so neither Theorem 2 nor Theorem 4 was derived from the source's gamma condition.

STATUS: closed. What follows is the current state, not a history.

  The growing-query form. dissimilarity_convergesInProbability_of_secondMoment_growing takes the number of queries as a function of the replicate count, so the response matrices live in a different space at each stage -- which is the whole point of Theorem 2, a sufficient condition for how fast m may grow -- and dissimilarity_convergesInProbability_of_gamma states it in the source's own terms. The threshold moves with the stage, so the Chebyshev bound needs v r / (m r)^2 to vanish, which the source's condition gives with a spare factor of 1/m; and stages with m r = 0 need no separate argument, since the dissimilarities vanish there so the bad event is empty while v r / (eta r)^2 is v r / 0 = 0 under Lean's division convention.

  The growing-model form. pointwise_dissimilarity_convergesInProbability_of_gamma does the same for Theorem 4, with the model collection growing as well: models are indexed by all of N and the pair is fixed, and the growing model count costs nothing because the conclusion is pointwise, so the union bound is over the two models in the pair rather than over n. sourceGammaRate_imp_secondMomentRate is the step both share.

  No rate shared by the collection. The bound is indexed by the model as well as by the stage, and each model's bound is required only eventually, at a stage of its own choosing. An earlier version of these theorems took one sequence S r and asked every model index to satisfy it, which is a uniformity over an infinite collection that the source does not state -- the paper attaches (1/m) sum_j gamma_ij to the model i -- and which is also the wrong shape for the reason the theorem is pointwise: only the two models of the pair are ever used. That was found in review and removed.

  Appendix A.2. Both theorems now also exist in a form that takes no second-moment hypothesis at all: dissimilarity_convergesInProbability_of_replicates and pointwise_dissimilarity_convergesInProbability_of_replicates start from the sampling model. The derivation is integral_norm_sq_matrix_le_sum_row_bounds: one query at a time by integral_norm_sq_sampleMean_sub_mean_le_of_bound, then summed over the rows of the response matrix. The row split is an identity (integral_norm_sq_eq_sum_query), so the responses to different queries are never asked to be independent of one another; only the replicates of a fixed query are, which is exactly what 'g(f_i(q_j)_k) ~iid F_ij' says. eventually_integral_norm_sq_le_sum_gamma packages it as the hypothesis the concentration theorems consume.

An earlier version of this entry called Theorem 2 closed and the rows exact while the second-moment bound was still an input; that was withdrawn, and discharging it is what the row-by-row derivation above does.

rigid-motion-engine-now-available.title: The distance-to-coordinates step now has an engine; the eigenvalue floor is needed only for rates
rigid-motion-engine-now-available.detail:
Acharyya2024.rawStress_mds_stability is eigengap-free -- its hypotheses are minimality, a unique pair profile, and dissimilarity convergence, with no spectral condition -- but it concludes convergence of pairwise distances rather than of coordinates. The missing step is Acharyya 2024 Corollary 1, and its exact form is now proved as TauCeti.exists_rigidMotion_of_dist_eq: equal pairwise distances imply the configurations differ by a rigid motion. Mathlib does not carry this; it has Congruent and the triangle criteria only.

What each paper needs from the bridge differs. Helm's conclusions are Tendsto statements with no rate, so the qualitative eigengap-free route suffices and its population eigenvalue floor is avoidable, modulo the approximate form of the rigidity lemma. Quench's capstones carry entryRate and GrowingConfigControl and conclude stagewise high-probability bounds; a quantitative Gram-to-configuration bound needs a spectral gap, because eigenvector perturbation is unstable without one, so Quench's floor is likely intrinsic rather than an artifact.

corollary1-deterministic-alignment.title: Corollary 1 quantifies the aligning rotation outside the probability -- REFUTED
corollary1-deterministic-alignment.detail:
FINDING. The source writes "there exist sequences W^(u) and a^(u), with W^(u) in O(d) and a^(u) in R^d, such that for all i, ||psihat_i^(r_u) - (W^(u) psi_i + a^(u))|| ->P 0". The alignment is quantified OUTSIDE the probability, so one deterministic pair per stage is asserted to serve every sample point. The estimate is a function of the sample and MDS fixes a configuration only up to a rigid motion, so the aligning motion is a function of the sample too.

REFUTED, with a machine-checked counterexample. Consistency.not_exists_deterministic_rigidMotion_of_pairDist_exact exhibits a dissimilarity matrix, a selection of its raw-stress minimizers, and a target minimizer, such that every pairwise distance is EXACTLY right at every stage -- the corollary's hypothesis in its strongest possible form -- and yet no sequence of orthogonal maps and translations gives convergence in probability of the coordinates. The selection returns a configuration on half the sample points and its reflection on the rest; both realize the matrix exactly, so both have zero raw stress and are genuine MDS outputs, which puts the counterexample inside the corollary's own setting rather than merely satisfying its arithmetic.

REPAIRED, in both modes. The alignment is chosen inside the probability, which is what a distance-based estimator can actually do. exists_rigidMotion_of_pairDist_tendsto is the deterministic step and needs no spectral hypothesis, so the eigengap-free raw-stress route reaches coordinates without a population eigenvalue floor. ae_eventually_exists_rigidMotion_of_ae_pairDist_tendsto gives the almost-sure mode. tendsto_measure_alignmentError_of_pairDist_convergesInProbability and tendsto_measure_alignedConfig_dist_gt give the in-probability mode, in the alignment-error and the coordinate form respectively.

An earlier version of this entry recorded the in-probability mode as blocked, on the grounds that the set of sample points admitting an eps-alignment is an existential over the isometry group and so not obviously measurable. That is resolved rather than outstanding, and by the route the entry itself proposed: TauCeti.alignmentError is the alignment error as an infimum over rigid motions, and TauCeti.exists_delta_forall_exists_rigidMotion supplies a modulus uniform over configurations, which is what a random target needs. Measurability turned out not to be required at all for the bound itself, since a measure is monotone and subadditive on arbitrary sets.

riemannian-structure-decorative.title: Assumption 2's Riemannian structure is not used by what Assumption 2 says
riemannian-structure-decorative.detail:
Assumption 2 introduces a compact Riemannian manifold M in an ambient R^q, but the distance on both sides of its limit is the AMBIENT norm: '(1/m)||mu_i - mu_i'|| -> ||phi_i - phi_i'||', and the dissimilarity function it induces is defined as 'Delta^(infinity)(phi_i, phi_i') = ||phi_i - phi_i'||', again the ambient norm rather than a geodesic distance. Nothing in the assumption's own statement refers to the Riemannian metric.

Compactness is likewise not used by what the assumption delivers. tendsto_frobSub_responseDist_of_ambientLimit derives the Frobenius convergence of the population dissimilarity matrices -- the hypothesis the growing-model chain consumes -- from the entrywise limits alone.

Both are recorded in the AmbientModelLimit structure so the assumption is represented at its printed scope; the manifold structure and the compactness are carried for the cited continuous-MDS theory downstream, where the model space genuinely matters, not for this step. This is a note about where the hypotheses do work, not a defect.

items.title: Finite raw-stress MDS objective and minimizer set
items.source_claim: For a finite dissimilarity matrix, define the raw-stress objective and MDS(Delta) as its minimizers in R^d.

semantic_alignment.detail: The Lean definitions directly encode the finite raw-stress objective and minimizer set.

items.notes: The package treats configurations as Fin n -> EuclideanSpace rather than matrices with rows.

items.title: Nonuniqueness and rigid/affine invariance of raw-stress minimizers
items.source_claim: Applying a rigid/affine transformation to a minimizer gives another minimizer; additional non-congruent minimizers may also exist.

semantic_alignment.detail: The invariance is now proved in full -- a rigid motion carries a minimizer to a minimizer -- rather than only its translation half. The source's description of the class as affine is corrected: raw stress sees only the pairwise distances, so a dilation changes it, and rawStress_not_affine_invariant exhibits that. The paper's Corollary 1 uses an orthogonal map plus a translation, so the intended class is the rigid one and the slip is in the wording of the remark.

items.notes: The remark's second clause, that non-congruent minimizers may also exist, is witnessed by ProfileNonuniqueness.no_fixed_limiting_profile, whose construction produces minimizers with distinct pairwise-distance profiles.
items.next_action: None. The invariance is proved at the correct class and the wording slip is recorded with a counterexample.

items.title: Existence of a finite raw-stress minimizer
items.source_claim: The finite raw-stress problem attains a minimizer.

semantic_alignment.detail: Lean proves nonemptiness directly for the finite raw-stress minimizer set, without requiring the source proof route through a bounded set of Euclidean distance matrices.

items.notes: The conclusion is the source conclusion; the proof architecture is different and the Lean statement is usable for arbitrary finite dissimilarity data.

items.title: Continuous MDS over a compact model space
items.source_claim: Define continuous raw stress by a P x P integral over a compact model space and let mds minimize it over Borel-measurable embeddings.

semantic_alignment.detail: The construction is present at the printed scope: continuousRawStress is the double integral against the model distribution, and ContinuousMDS is the set of Borel-measurable embeddings minimizing it over all Borel-measurable embeddings, which is the faithful reading of "the embedding function that minimizes" -- as with the finite MDS, the minimizer is determined only up to a rigid motion. The Lean definition does not require the model space to be compact; compactness enters the source only for existence of the minimizer, which the source itself attributes to the cited literature.

items.notes: continuousRawStress_empiricalPopulation ties the definition to the package's finite rawStress through the empirical measure, so it is not a parallel notion.
items.next_action: None. This row is the construction, and it is complete; the L^p limit theorem stated over it is A24-L2's and A24-T5's business, and is tracked there.

items.title: Notation for the replicate dependence of the estimated perspectives
items.source_claim: In every setting r -> infinity; for quantities whose definition depends on r, such as psi-hat, the dependence is sometimes written psi-hat^(r).

semantic_alignment.detail: A notational convention introducing the superscript r, with no mathematical content to formalize. The r-dependence it names is carried explicitly by the stage index in every Lean statement, so the convention is honoured without a declaration.

items.notes: Included so the census covers every numbered source item; an adversarial reviewer should be able to see that this remark was read and classified, not skipped.

items.title: Fixed models and fixed queries: raw-stress consistency
items.source_claim: With n and m fixed, a subsequence of estimated raw-stress minimizers has pairwise distances converging in probability to those of a fixed population minimizer.

semantic_alignment.detail: The printed statement names a fixed limiting minimizer with no uniqueness premise, and that is false: no_fixed_limiting_profile is a counterexample satisfying every printed hypothesis in its strongest form. RawStress.UniquePairProfile is the repair, and in exchange the Lean conclusion holds along the full sequence rather than along a subsequence, which is stronger than printed. The unconditional content -- convergence to the minimizer SET -- is separately proved without any uniqueness premise by rawStress_mds_stability_set.

items.notes: The repaired theorem actually proves the fixed-profile convergence along the full sequence and then supplies id as the source subsequence.
items.next_action: None. The printed statement is refuted, the repair is proved, and the premise-free set form is available alongside it.

items.title: Finite-model population dissimilarities have a fixed Euclidean limit
items.source_claim: For fixed models there are vectors phi_i in a finite-dimensional Euclidean space whose pairwise distances are the limits of the population model-mean discrepancies as m,r grow.

semantic_alignment.detail: The active theorem only needs deterministic convergence of the population dissimilarity matrices to a fixed DeltaInf; for fixed n entrywise convergence suffices. It does not require that DeltaInf be represented by named phi_i vectors.

items.notes: This weakens the structural content of the paper assumption to the part actually used by the proof.

items.title: Raw-stress stability under convergence of dissimilarity matrices
items.source_claim: If D converges to Delta^(infinity) with n fixed, a subsequence of MDS(D) has pairwise distances converging to those of a fixed minimizer of MDS(Delta^(infinity)).

semantic_alignment.detail: The printed statement names a fixed limiting minimizer with no uniqueness premise, and that is false: no_fixed_limiting_profile is a counterexample satisfying every printed hypothesis in its strongest form. RawStress.UniquePairProfile is the repair, and in exchange the Lean conclusion holds along the full sequence rather than along a subsequence, which is stronger than printed. The unconditional content -- convergence to the minimizer SET -- is separately proved without any uniqueness premise by rawStress_mds_stability_set.

items.notes: The set-valued theorem isolates the strongest unconditional statement.
items.next_action: None. The printed statement is refuted, the repair is proved, and the premise-free set form is available alongside it.

items.title: Dissimilarity concentration under the covariance-trace rate
items.source_claim: If (1/m) sum_j gamma_ij / r tends to zero for every fixed model, then the empirical dissimilarity matrix converges in Frobenius norm in probability to Delta^(infinity).

semantic_alignment.detail:
dissimilarity_convergesInProbability_of_replicates is the printed theorem end to end: the number of queries is a function of the replicate count, gamma_ij is the trace-covariance of the response of model i to query j, the hypothesis is the source's ((1/m) sum_j gamma_ij)/r -> 0, and the conclusion is convergence of the Frobenius distance in probability. The sample-mean second-moment bound is no longer an input: it is derived, which is the content of the source's Appendix A.2. integral_norm_sq_matrix_le_sum_row_bounds is that derivation for the response matrix -- one query at a time by integral_norm_sq_sampleMean_sub_mean_le_of_bound, then summed over rows. The row sum is an identity (integral_norm_sq_eq_sum_query), so the responses to different queries are never asked to be independent of one another; only the replicates of a fixed query are, which is what 'g(f_i(q_j)_k) ~iid F_ij' says.

dissimilarity_convergesInProbability_of_gamma remains as the intermediate form that takes the second-moment bound as a hypothesis, and the fixed-m form remains for the downstream finite theorems.

items.notes: The fixed-m form remains available and is what the downstream finite theorems consume. The moment hypothesis of the intermediate forms is now required only eventually: at r = 0 the printed rate gamma/r is not a bound on anything, and demanding it there was an artifact.

items.title: Fixed models, growing queries: DKPS consistency
items.source_claim: Under the Theorem 2 rate condition, estimated raw-stress pairwise distances converge along a subsequence to a population MDS configuration.

semantic_alignment.detail: The printed statement names a fixed limiting minimizer with no uniqueness premise, and that is false: no_fixed_limiting_profile is a counterexample satisfying every printed hypothesis in its strongest form. RawStress.UniquePairProfile is the repair, and in exchange the Lean conclusion holds along the full sequence rather than along a subsequence, which is stronger than printed. The unconditional content -- convergence to the minimizer SET -- is separately proved without any uniqueness premise by rawStress_mds_stability_set.

items.notes: Under the added uniqueness premise the Lean proof obtains full-sequence convergence.
items.next_action: None. The printed statement is refuted, the repair is proved, and the premise-free set form is available alongside it.

items.title: Coordinate convergence after orthogonal alignment and translation
items.source_claim: There exist orthogonal W^(u) and translations a^(u) such that every estimated point converges in probability to W^(u) psi_i + a^(u).

semantic_alignment.detail: The corollary as printed places the orthogonal map and the translation outside the probability, one per stage, serving every sample point. That is false, and the refutation is machine-checked: a legitimate selection of raw-stress minimizers can return a reflected copy on some sample points and the original on others, matching every pairwise distance exactly while admitting no common alignment. The repair chooses the motion inside the probability and is proved in both the alignment-error and the coordinate form, in probability as well as almost surely. Every other clause of the corollary is met at the printed scope.

items.notes: The alignment error -- the least uniform distance to the target achievable by a rigid motion -- is the quantity that converges. Its existence needs no measurability of the estimates, since a measure is monotone and subadditive on arbitrary sets.
items.next_action: None. The printed statement is refuted and the repair is proved; retain the counterexample as the record of why the alignment must sit inside the probability.

items.title: Growing models lie on a compact Riemannian model manifold
items.source_claim: There is a compact Riemannian manifold M containing latent vectors phi_i whose pairwise distances are the limiting model dissimilarities.

semantic_alignment.detail: AmbientModelLimit is the assumption at its printed scope: a compact model space in an ambient Euclidean space, a latent vector in it for each model, and convergence of the normalized population dissimilarities to the ambient pairwise distances. limitDissimilarity is the induced Delta^(infinity), which the source defines as the ambient norm. The Riemannian structure is not referred to by the assumption's own statement and compactness is not consumed by what it delivers; both are recorded and the note explains where they do work.

items.notes: lp_consistency_of_gamma_ambientLimit feeds the assumption directly into the growing-model L^p chain, so it is represented in use and not only as a definition.
items.next_action: None. The remaining growing-model gap is the population law in Lemma 2 and Theorem 5, not this assumption.

items.title: Continuous-MDS L^p stability over iid model draws
items.source_claim: For iid phi_i from P, pointwise convergence of empirical dissimilarities implies, along a subsequence, L^p(P x P) convergence of estimated pairwise distances to continuous-MDS distances.

semantic_alignment.detail:
The printed lemma's estimate is fitted to the SAMPLE dissimilarities D under the hypothesis that D approaches the population Delta, and that is what tendsto_measure_lpPairDistErr_sampleTarget proves: the estimate minimizes the one-point stress against a target that changes with the stage, and the L^p(P x P) discrepancy against the population embedding tends to zero in probability along a subsequence. exists_subseq_tendsto_measure_lpPairDistErr_of_identical states the same conclusion from hypotheses on the dissimilarities alone and produces the subsequence itself, and the subsequence is independent of the tolerance, as printed. One clause is stronger than printed: one statement in p rather than one per p.

Two clauses are repairs and each carries a compiled witness of its necessity. First, the printed hypothesis -- pointwise convergence in probability at each pair -- does not control a growing collection: TauCeti.exists_triangular_array_tendsto_pointwise_average_eq_half exhibits a bounded array whose entries are eventually zero at every fixed index while the average is exactly one half at every stage. What repairs it is that the per-stage errors have a common mean, and that is now a THEOREM rather than a hypothesis: integral_absPairErr_eq_of_dissimilarityFactors derives it from the source's own definition of D as a statistic of the two models involved, together with the reference models being drawn independently from a common law; exists_subseq_tendsto_measure_lpPairDistErr_of_pairwise is the lemma with the factorization in place of the identical-distribution assumption. The residual repair is in the sampling model, not in the estimate: the source draws phi_i ~iid P and leaves the response laws F_ij attached to the model, so what the argument needs is that a MODEL is drawn as a complete object, not merely its latent vector. Some repair is forced -- the printed conclusion's integrand depends on the estimate and hence on the response data, so it does not denote anything under a measure carrying only the latent vector -- but this particular repair, augmenting the inner population measure by the response outcome, is a choice, not the unique minimal one; see A24-T5 for the alternative that was not taken. Second, the limiting one-point stress is assumed to have a unique minimizer; Consistency.not_unique_min_continuousPointStress shows that premise cannot be dropped. Estimator measurability is what the printed integral needs to denote anything.

The population-target form tendsto_measure_lpPairDistErr_outOfSample remains proved separately, along the full sequence -- that is the continuous-MDS identification the source attributes to its reference [23].

items.notes: The source attributes this lemma to its reference [23]. Both halves are proved here: the continuous-MDS identification against the population dissimilarities, and the perturbation to the sample dissimilarities that the printed statement actually makes. The identically-distributed hypothesis is no longer an assumption of the lemma's usable form; it is derived from the source's definition of D.
items.next_action: None. The estimate is fitted to the sample dissimilarities, the printed subsequence is derived rather than assumed and does not depend on the tolerance, the common-mean hypothesis is derived from the source's own D, and the remaining repair -- drawing a model rather than only its latent vector -- is stated explicitly and is what makes the printed conclusion well defined.

items.title: Growing-model pointwise dissimilarity concentration
items.source_claim: When n,m grow with r, the same covariance-trace rate implies pointwise convergence D_ii' -> Delta^(infinity)(phi_i,phi_i') in probability for every fixed pair.

semantic_alignment.detail:
The printed theorem: models indexed by all of N so their number grows, the number of queries a function of the replicate count, the same trace-covariance condition, and pointwise convergence in probability for a fixed pair. The growing model count costs nothing because the conclusion is pointwise: the union bound is over the two models in the pair, not over n.

Nothing in the chain is shared across the model collection. Each model k carries its own bound S k = sum_j gamma_kj and its own rate, and the proof uses them only at i and i'; a single sequence bounding every model would be a uniformity the source does not state, since the paper attaches (1/m) sum_j gamma_ij to the model i. Each model's moment bound is also required only eventually, at a stage of its own choosing.

pointwise_dissimilarity_convergesInProbability_of_replicates is the theorem from the sampling model with no second-moment hypothesis at all: Appendix A.2 is discharged by integral_norm_sq_matrix_le_sum_row_bounds, row by row over the queries, assuming replicate independence for each fixed query and nothing across queries.

The theorem also exists in the form Theorem 5 needs, with the models themselves drawn. pointwise_dissimilarity_convergesInProbability_of_gamma_kernel states it under a Markov kernel, which is the source's own sampling model -- the response distributions F_ij belong to the model, so the law of the replicates depends on which models were drawn -- and reads the paper's condition almost surely in the draw. No bound uniform over the model population enters: the conditional bad-event probabilities lie in [0, 1], so the constant 1 dominates them and the model integral passes through the limit (TauCeti.tendsto_measure_compProd_gt_of_ae_tendsto_measure_slice). pairwise_dissimilarity_convergesInProbability_of_gamma is the two-model form Lemma 2 consumes, and it combines the two drawn models' own bounds only after the pair is fixed; the regrouping of an independent pair of two-stage experiments into one two-stage experiment on the pair is TauCeti.map_shuffle_prod_compProd.

items.notes: An earlier pass recorded this row as by_composition because the second-moment bound was an input. It is now derived. That pass also left a single bound S r covering every model index, which was a uniformity over an infinite collection that the source does not state; the bound is now indexed by the model.

items.title: Growing models and queries: L^p consistency
items.source_claim: Under the Theorem 4 rate, along a subsequence the pairwise-distance error converges to zero in L^p(P x P) in probability for every p >= 1.

semantic_alignment.detail:
Theorem 5 is the composition 'Theorem 4, then Lemma 2', and it is assembled over the population law the printed theorem draws from: lp_consistency_of_gamma_population takes the source's trace-covariance condition -- read almost surely in the model draw, which is what 'for all i in N' means once the models are random -- together with Assumption 2 and the standing structural hypotheses of Lemma 2, and concludes that along a subsequence the L^p(P x P) discrepancy tends to zero in probability. The subsequence does not depend on the tolerance. lp_consistency_of_replicates_population is the same endpoint with the second-moment bound derived from the sampling model rather than assumed, so the theorem starts from the paper's replicates and gamma. Two clauses come out stronger than printed: every positive exponent rather than p >= 1, and, on the empirical-measure route (lp_consistency_of_gamma_empirical), the full sequence rather than a subsequence.

The three passages the composition needs are proved rather than assumed. (i) Theorem 4 fixes the models and randomises the replicates while Lemma 2 draws the models; the conditional bad-event probabilities integrate over the draw by domination by 1, so NO uniformity over the model population and no uniform integrability of the gamma condition is required -- an earlier reading of this row asserted such a requirement, and it was an artifact of routing through an integrated second-moment bound. (ii) A fresh query paired with a drawn reference and two distinct drawn references have the same law P x P (measure_absPairErr_query_eq, measure_absPairErr_sampled_eq), so Theorem 4's conclusion is literally Lemma 2's hypothesis. (iii) The per-index errors have a common mean because the source's D is a statistic of the two models involved (integral_absPairErr_eq_of_dissimilarityFactors).

THE REPAIR, STATED PRECISELY. The measure the conclusion integrates against is P = Pmod (x) kappa: the law of a model TOGETHER WITH a realized response-data outcome. The paper writes P(dphi) on the latent/model space and declares phi_i ~iid P, while the estimate inside the integrand depends on the model-specific response laws F_ij and on the sampled responses, so the printed display does not denote anything under a measure carrying only the latent vector. Some repair is therefore forced. The one chosen here augments the inner population measure by the response outcome, and it is the one under which hid is a theorem rather than an assumption. It is NOT claimed to be the unique minimal reading: an alternative formalization could keep P on the model space and place a random response field in the outer probability space instead. That reading is considerably more cumbersome and is not formalized here; the disposition records which repaired reading was chosen, not that no other exists.

items.notes: The empirical-measure composition lp_consistency_of_gamma_empirical remains, along the full sequence. lp_consistency_of_gamma_population is the printed statement over the augmented model-and-data population law, and lp_consistency_of_replicates_population derives its second-moment hypothesis from the sampling model. The claim that composing Theorem 4 with Lemma 2 needs a uniformity condition the source does not state has been withdrawn: it is not needed.
